PURPOSE. The page carries out a harmonic (cosine-Fourier) analysis of a 25-value table f_0..f_24. The values are given in units of 1e-7, at x_k = 7.5k degrees, from 0 to 180 degrees. Treating f as an even 360-degree-periodic function (48 points per period), Gauss wants the coefficients a_n in f(x) = sum a_n cos(n x).

The data rise monotonically from 2.5778036 to 3.0004806. The previous page tabulates, on the same 7.5-degree grid, a root x(phi) of an equation in cos(phi). It gives x ~ cbrt(16) +/- sqrt((203.80968 - 200 cos(phi))/(672 cbrt(4))), whose lower branch is about 2.460 at phi=0. Here f_0 = 2.5778 is close to the upper branch (2.5796), and f_0 plus the previous page's 2.4580892 is about 5.036, near 2 cbrt(16) = 5.0397. So this table is plausibly the companion root of the same problem. That identification is my conjecture.

The method is repeated folding by sums and differences, followed by multiplication with the exact values of cos 15, 30, 45, 60, 75 degrees.

(1) FIRST FOLD. Row 1 holds f_0..f_12; row 2 holds f_24, f_23, ..., f_13, written under f_0..f_11.
- s_k = f_k + f_{24-k} (k=0..11), s_12 = 2 f_12. These are rows 3-4, the latter written in reverse order s_12..s_7.
- d_k = f_k - f_{24-k} (k=0..11) appear lower left and lower middle.
- Even k: d0 = -4226770, d2 = -3824114, d4 = -3114017, d6 = -2349955, d8 = -1570910, d10 = -786419.
- Odd k, lettered: alpha = -4104585, beta = -3481503, gamma = -2735006, delta = -1961467, epsilon = -1179064, zeta = -393315.
- The s_k carry the even harmonics; the d_k carry the odd harmonics, since d(x) = 2 sum_{n odd} a_n cos(n x).

(2) EVEN HARMONICS.
- Second fold: t_k = s_k + s_{12-k}, with t_6 = 2 s_6 (rows 5-6). Also u_k = s_k - s_{12-k}: u0..u5 = -1860972, -1739072, -1459523, -1118597, -753785, -378843.
- Third fold: v_k = t_k + t_{6-k}, with v_3 = 2 t_3, giving 227561486, 227621625, 227717318, 227757254. Also w_k = t_k - t_{6-k}: w0, w1, w2 = -708174, -589189, -319552 (the last should carry a minus sign).
- Constant term: v0+v3 = 455318740 and v1+v2 = 455338943. Then 1365996626 = (v0+v3) + 2(v1+v2), which is twice the trapezoid sum. Hence a0 = 1365996626/48 = 28458263 (mean value 2.8458; division mine).
- Further differences: -20201 = (v0+v3)-(v1+v2), -195768 = v0-v3, -95697 = v1-v2, and 291461 (origin unclear).
- n = 4 mod 8 group: w0+w2 = -1027726, so -1027726/24 = -42821.92. Next, log 589189 = 5.7702547 and 1.1416506 = log(8 sqrt3), so w1 sqrt3/24 = -42521.06. Thus a4-type sum = -42821.92 - 42521.06 and a20-type = their difference (not formed on the page). Also 69070 = 2|w2| - |w0| (that is, -(w0 - 2w2)), which belongs to n = 12.
- n = 2 mod 4 group (u_k), even-k part: (u0+u4)/24 = -2614757/24 = -108948.21. Then u2 sqrt3/24 = u2/(8 sqrt3): log 1459523 = 6.1642110, minus 1.1416506, gives -105332.01. Sum for n=2: -214280.22. Difference for n=10: -3616.20.
- Same group, odd-k part: (u1+u5) sqrt6/48 = -2117915/(8 sqrt6), using 1.2921656 = log(8 sqrt6), gives -108079.43. Then (u1-u5+2u3) sqrt2/48 = -3597423/(24 sqrt2), using 1.5307262 = log(24 sqrt2), gives -105990.10. Sum (n=2) = -214069.5. Difference (n=10) = -2089.3.
- n = 6: even part (u0/2 - u4)/12 = -14725.08. Odd part (u1-u3-u5) sqrt2/24 = -241632/(12 sqrt2) = -14238.3, using 1.2296962 = log(12 sqrt2).

(3) ODD HARMONICS. For odd n, a_n (with its alias a_{24-n}) = E_n + O_n, where E_n = (1/12)[d0/2 + sum over even k>=2 of d_k cos(n x_k)] and O_n = (1/12) sum over odd k of d_k cos(n x_k). Also E_n - O_n gives the alias a_{24-n} (my normalization).

Even-k part, using cos15 = (sqrt6+sqrt2)/4 and cos75 = (sqrt6-sqrt2)/4:
- (d0+d8)/24 = -5797680/24 = -241570.00.
- d4 sqrt3/24: log 3114017 = 6.4933210, minus log(8 sqrt3), gives -224734.82.
- (d2+d10) sqrt6/48: log 4610533 = 6.6637511, minus log(8 sqrt6), gives -235280.27.
- (d2-d10+2d6) sqrt2/48 = -7737605/(24 sqrt2) = -227971.42.
- Grouping: P1 = -241570.00 - 224734.82 = -466304.82 and Q1 = -235280.27 - 227971.42 = -463251.69. So E1 = P1+Q1 = -929556.51 and E11 = P1-Q1 = -3053.13.
- P3 = (d0/2 - d8)/12 = -1084950/24 = -45206.25. Q3 = (d2-d6-d10) sqrt2/24 = -687740/(12 sqrt2) = -40525.48 (log 5.8374243). So E3 = -85731.73 and E9 = -4680.77.
- P5 = -241570 + 224734.82 = -16835.18. Q5 = -235280.27 + 227971.42 = -7308.85. So E5 = -24144.03 and E7 = -9526.33.

Odd-k part, by combinations of the lettered values and auxiliary angles:
- Pair (3,9): 12 O3 = cos22.5 (alpha-delta-epsilon) + sin22.5 (beta-gamma-zeta), and 12 O9 = sin22.5 (alpha-delta-epsilon) - cos22.5 (beta-gamma-zeta).
  - Here alpha-delta-epsilon = -964054 and beta-gamma-zeta = -353182.
  - Put R cos(theta) = -964054 and R sin(theta) = -353182. Then theta = 200 deg 7'13.60", log cos(theta) = 9.9726524, log R = 6.0114490.
  - Divide by 12 (log 1.0791812), then multiply by cos and sin of phi = 382.5 - theta = 182 deg 22'46.40".
  - Result: O3 = -85485.63 and O9 = -3552.35.
- Pairs (1,7) and (5,11): use cos7.5 = (sqrt3/2)cos22.5 + (1/2)sin22.5, cos52.5 = (sqrt3/2)cos22.5 - (1/2)sin22.5, cos37.5 = (1/2)cos22.5 + (sqrt3/2)sin22.5, cos82.5 = (1/2)cos22.5 - (sqrt3/2)sin22.5. This gives 12 O1 = (sqrt3/2)[(alpha+delta)cos22.5 + (gamma-zeta)sin22.5] + (1/2)[(2beta+gamma+zeta)cos22.5 + (alpha-delta+2epsilon)sin22.5].
  - First bracket: alpha+delta = -6066052 and gamma-zeta = -2341691. theta = 201 deg 6'29" 31/63, log R = 6.8130701. Dividing by 8 sqrt3 gives 5.6714195.
  - With phi = 382.5 - theta = 181 deg 23'30" 32/63 this yields A = -469127.96 (cos part) and C = -11398.12 (sin part).
  - Second bracket: 2beta = -6963006, gamma+zeta = -3128321, alpha-delta = -2143118, 2epsilon = -2358128. So 2beta+gamma+zeta = -10091327 and alpha-delta+2epsilon = -4501246.
  - These give theta' = 245 deg 57'38" 16/37 (Gauss takes tan theta' = 10091327/4501246), log cos 24.04 = 9.9605974, log R = 7.0433509. Dividing by 24 gives 5.6631397.
  - With phi = 427.5 - theta' = 181 deg 32'21" 31/37 this yields B = -460238.92 and D = -12367.82.
- Then O1 = A+B = -929366.88, O7 = A-B = -8889.04, O5 = C+D = -23765.94, and O11 = (C-D, sign as written) -969.70.

Result rows: E_n = -929556.51, -85731.73, -24144.03, -9526.33, -4680.77, -3053.13 and O_n = -929366.88, -85485.63, -23765.94, -8889.04, -3552.35, -969.70 for n = 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11.

The final step is not on the page (mine): a_1 = E1+O1 = -1858923 (i.e. -0.1858923) and alias a_23 = E1-O1 = -190, and similarly for the other n.

results.what: Cosine coefficients of a 48-point periodic (25-value half-period) table by successive sum/difference folding f_k +/- f_{24-k}, s_k +/- s_{12-k}, t_k +/- t_{6-k}, separating harmonic classes mod 2, 4, 8
results.modern_name: Discrete Fourier/trigonometric interpolation via symmetric folding; radix-2 decimation, essentially a Runge-type computing scheme and an FFT-like factorization
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Theoria interpolationis, c.1805, publ. Werke III 1866) for trigonometric interpolation and FFT idea; practical schemes to Runge (1903), Runge-Koenig; FFT to Cooley-Tukey 1965

results.what: Pairing of aliased coefficients: even-sample and odd-sample partial sums E_n, O_n give a_n = E_n+O_n and a_{24-n} = E_n-O_n; pairs (1,11),(3,9),(5,7) for even k and (1,7),(3,9),(5,11) for odd k
Use of auxiliary angle phi = 22.5 deg (or 67.5 deg) - theta to obtain two harmonic sums (e.g. O3 and O9) from one polar conversion via logarithms
results.modern_name: Auxiliary-angle (harmonic addition) trick in logarithmic computation

results.what: Exact reduction of cos 7.5k deg and cos 15k deg multipliers to sqrt2, sqrt3, sqrt6 factors (logs of 8sqrt3, 8sqrt6, 12sqrt2, 24sqrt2)
results.modern_name: Exact trigonometric values in harmonic analysis

deep.surprise_reason: This is a carefully organised numerical harmonic analysis with 24 subdivisions of the half period, folding into residue classes and exploiting aliasing. It is effectively an FFT-style factorization, but Gauss's authorship of trigonometric interpolation and FFT-like decomposition is already well documented (Theoria interpolationis; Heideman-Johnson-Burrus 1984). The worked 48-point example is a nice unpublished detail of practice, not a new result.
